manifests.title: Quantity dependency map
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: A rental costs $18 plus $7 per hour. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: C(h)=18+7h dollars.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify the input, output, parameters, and units in a quantitative relationship and explain how the quantities depend on one another.

manifests.title: Parameter family graph
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Define every quantity and unit, identify the direction of dependency, and check that terms combined in a formula have compatible units. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify the input, output, parameters, and units in a quantitative relationship and explain how the quantities depend on one another.

manifests.title: Unit consistency ledger
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is manipulating symbols before defining what they measure. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify the input, output, parameters, and units in a quantitative relationship and explain how the quantities depend on one another.

manifests.title: Mapping comparison
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Does (0,3),(1,5),(2,5),(3,8) define a function? Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Yes. Every input has one output.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine whether a relation is a function by applying the rule that each allowed input has exactly one output.

manifests.title: Vertical-line derivation
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Check repeated inputs in a table, outgoing arrows in a mapping, vertical intersections in a graph, or the rule stated by a context. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine whether a relation is a function by applying the rule that each allowed input has exactly one output.

manifests.title: Discrete and continuous functions
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is rejecting a many-to-one function because an output repeats. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine whether a relation is a function by applying the rule that each allowed input has exactly one output.

manifests.title: Vertical versus horizontal tracing
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: For f(x)=2x^2-3x, find f(-2). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: 14.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use function notation accurately and distinguish finding an output from finding inputs that produce a chosen output.

manifests.title: Substitution grouping
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Substitute the entire input with parentheses or trace the input through a table or graph. For f(x)=k, solve for every preimage. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use function notation accurately and distinguish finding an output from finding inputs that produce a chosen output.

manifests.title: Preimage set
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is confusing f(a) with the equation f(x)=a. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use function notation accurately and distinguish finding an output from finding inputs that produce a chosen output.

manifests.title: Four-representation dashboard
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Values 5,8,11,14 occur at x=0,1,2,3. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: A linear candidate is f(x)=3x+5.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Translate a function relationship among verbal, tabular, graphical, and algebraic representations while preserving quantities, units, and domain.

manifests.title: Discrete versus continuous connection
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Translate one representation at a time while preserving input, output, units, and domain; then verify agreement at shared values. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Translate a function relationship among verbal, tabular, graphical, and algebraic representations while preserving quantities, units, and domain.

manifests.title: Exact rule versus fitted model
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is inventing continuity or a unique formula from a small table. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Translate a function relationship among verbal, tabular, graphical, and algebraic representations while preserving quantities, units, and domain.

manifests.title: Restriction icons
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Find domain of ln(x-1)/sqrt(x+2). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: x>1.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine the real domain of a function by combining denominator, even-root, logarithm, and composition restrictions.

manifests.title: Condition intersection
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Write each restriction separately, solve it, intersect the solution sets, and retain exclusions hidden by cancellation. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine the real domain of a function by combining denominator, even-root, logarithm, and composition restrictions.

manifests.title: Retained hole
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is checking only one restriction or using the simplified formula's larger domain. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine the real domain of a function by combining denominator, even-root, logarithm, and composition restrictions.

manifests.title: Nested domains
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: A theater has capacity 240 and R(n)=12n. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: n is an integer from 0 through 240.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Distinguish the algebraic domain of a formula from the inputs that are meaningful in a model.

manifests.title: Discrete versus continuous domains
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Begin with the algebraic domain, then apply nonnegativity, capacity, integer, safety, time-window, and evidence-range restrictions. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Distinguish the algebraic domain of a formula from the inputs that are meaningful in a model.

manifests.title: Extrapolation warning
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is reporting all real numbers for a model involving time, length, population, or counts. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Distinguish the algebraic domain of a formula from the inputs that are meaningful in a model.

manifests.title: Domain-range projections
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: A graph has included minimum -3 and no upper bound. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Range [-3,∞).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Read range, intercepts, extrema, boundedness, symmetry, and intervals of increase or decrease from a graph.

manifests.title: Behavior intervals
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Project onto the axes for domain and range, label intercepts as points, and report increase or decrease intervals with input values. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Read range, intercepts, extrema, boundedness, symmetry, and intervals of increase or decrease from a graph.

manifests.title: Local versus absolute extrema
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is writing outputs as intervals of increase or calling every local peak an absolute maximum. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Read range, intercepts, extrema, boundedness, symmetry, and intervals of increase or decrease from a graph.

manifests.title: Piecewise rule selector
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: f=x+2 for x<1 and x^2 for x≥1; find f(-3),f(1),f(2). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: -1,1,4.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Evaluate, graph, and interpret functions that use different rules on different parts of the domain.

manifests.title: Endpoint gallery
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Locate the input interval first, evaluate with that rule, and graph each restricted piece with correct open or closed endpoints. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Evaluate, graph, and interpret functions that use different rules on different parts of the domain.

manifests.title: Boundary behavior comparison
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is evaluating every formula or including both boundary points. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Evaluate, graph, and interpret functions that use different rules on different parts of the domain.

manifests.title: Movable secant
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Find average rate of x^2 from 1 to 4. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: 5.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.

manifests.title: Same average, different paths
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Evaluate both endpoints, subtract in matching order, simplify, attach compound units, and interpret the sign over the interval. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.

manifests.title: Interval-dependent secants
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is reversing only one difference or omitting units. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.

manifests.title: Modeling cycle
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Costs 65,90,115,140 for 1-4 hours. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: C(h)=40+25h.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations.

manifests.title: Competing extrapolations
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Define quantities, choose a family, estimate parameters, state domain and assumptions, inspect residuals, and revise or reject when evidence disagrees. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations.

manifests.title: Residual plot
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is choosing the smoothest graph or highest fit statistic without checking meaning. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct, compare, and defend function representations while stating assumptions, domain, units, and limitations.
